title: A Drop for the Cover
premise: Gideon Reyes, a ghost negotiator who works the cases agencies can't admit to, receives a calendar invite from Marcus Hale—the handler she failed to save three years ago, dated for tomorrow. Following it leads her into a buried program called COVER, which trained negotiators like her and then erased them when they became liabilities. As Gideon unravels who sent the invite and why Hale's death was staged, she discovers the network is hunting its remaining graduates one by one, and that her own memory of the failure that defines her has been edited. To end it, Gideon must turn the program's own negotiation tactics against its architect—accepting that justice means exposing herself, her real name, and the truth about the night Hale died.
about_author: Astrid Vasquez spent a decade in crisis communications before turning to fiction, drawn to the people who talk others back from the edge. She writes from a coastal town she refuses to name, where she collects unsolved-case podcasts and strong coffee.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Working an anonymous hostage case in a shuttered mall, Gideon receives a meeting request from Marcus Hale—dead three years, timestamped tomorrow at dawn. She finishes the negotiation flawlessly and walks away shaken, checking the obituary she knows by heart. Emotional beat: the crack in her controlled invisibility; someone knows exactly who she is.

chapters.title: Dawn at the Dead Drop
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. She goes to the meeting site—a decommissioned radio station—and finds no Hale, only his voice on a looped recording naming COVER and warning 'they're finishing the roster.' A second graduate, Ilsa Brandt, is found dead hours later, staged as suicide. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into purpose; Gideon chooses to investigate instead of run.

chapters.title: What the Board Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Gideon, with a flashback interlude. She audits her own memory of the failed negotiation that got Hale killed and finds seams—details that don't match her recollection, a missing forty minutes. Her old contact, records clerk Danny Okafor, confirms her file was altered. Emotional beat: vertigo; the self she built on guilt may be built on fiction.

chapters.title: The Roster
chapters.summary: POV alternating Gideon and the antagonist, known only as 'Auditor.' Gideon identifies four surviving COVER graduates; two are already dead. The Auditor reviews targets with bureaucratic calm, revealing the program's logic: witnesses to an illegal op are being closed out. Emotional beat: dread through symmetry—hunter and hunted running parallel checklists.

chapters.title: A Voice on the Line
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Gideon reaches survivor Tomas Vega, now a small-town police captain, and talks him off the ledge of paranoia long enough to compare memories. Their accounts of the same training differ in ways that prove systematic memory editing. Emotional beat: fragile belonging—two ghosts recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Counteroffer
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. The Auditor contacts Gideon directly, offering reinstatement, protection, and restored memories in exchange for the names of the other survivors. She stalls him using his own techniques against him, buying time while Danny digs into funding trails. Emotional beat: temptation and contempt; she realizes the offer itself confirms they fear what she remembers.

chapters.title: Forty Minutes
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Danny recovers the redacted segment: Hale wasn't lost to Gideon's failure—he was executed by COVER during the negotiation, and her memory was rewritten to bury the evidence. The Auditor's team hits Danny's office; Danny barely escapes with the drive. Emotional beat: rage replacing guilt; the failure on her board was never hers.

chapters.title: The Last Graduate
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Vega is taken by the Auditor's team as bait. Gideon negotiates his release over an open line, deliberately revealing herself as the final name on the roster to draw the Auditor into the open. Emotional beat: sacrifice inverted—she spends her invisibility like currency to buy a life.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: POV Gideon, climax. At the original COVER training facility, Gideon faces the Auditor—who turns out to be Hale's superior and the architect of both the program and Hale's death. She runs a live negotiation with lives, evidence, and her own identity as stakes, forcing him to confess on record by convincing him surrender is his only exit. Emotional beat: cold clarity; every skill they gave her turned home.

chapters.title: A Name on the Record
chapters.summary: POV Gideon, resolution. The recordings go public; COVER burns, and survivors including Vega begin reclaiming their real histories. Gideon testifies under her true name, grieving Hale properly for the first time, and takes a legitimate post training negotiators openly. Emotional beat: belonging earned not by erasure but by standing visible in the light.
